# Step 4 independent benchmark

**Design approved on 25 November 2026.** The owner approved the six pairs, seven runs, movement register and proposed settings. The [frozen settings](thresholds.yaml) use the same values. D9 requires a second decision on the built packages, independently calculated answer key and checksums before the official benchmark is scored.

[Revision 2, R-031–R-034 and D9](../../docs/spec.md#benchmark-and-release-decision) defines the population and release metrics. D7 governs materiality, D6 the strength of financial conclusions, and D8 the evidence each result must carry. Use the [2.8.2 verification notes](../../mappings/VERIFICATION.md), [versioned mapping data](../../mappings/2.8.2/) and [normalized workbook layout](../../docs/input-format.md). The builder and answer key must never read or import the tool's source. Only the runner invokes its CLI and inspects its public outputs.

## What constitutes a package

One benchmark package is one named directory containing an **opening and a closing workbook** for one invented solo life insurer. Use 31 December 2024 and 31 December 2025, annual supervisory Standard Formula, base 2.8.2 at both dates, EUR, and a distinct synthetic name and checksum-valid invented LEI per pair. Each workbook declares its own metadata, dimensions, units and reporting precision. Use the whole undertaking, no RFF/MAP or accepted reinsurance, and explicit reported zeros where those facts support a comparison. A physical omission, a grey intersection and a reported zero have different meanings. Use explicit ratio precision 0.0001 in ratio units. Amounts in the illustrations below are EUR unless specified.

In a complete pair include S.01.01/S.01.02 metadata or equivalent cited declarations and filing statuses, S.02.01, S.12.01, S.23.01, S.25.01 and the S.05.01/S.22.01 schedules used for flags and controls. Include mapped S.26 drill-down in case 1 to test that headline SCR is invariant. For absence in case 3, make the filing inventory agree with the omission. Each case has its own `expected.yaml`. A confirmed reviewer decision in 2a is a sidecar on the same inputs. Mutated copies are outside the release population.

| Case and package | Scored run(s) | Deliberate observations and acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Clean annual solo close | 01-clean | All gate and applicable within-date checks pass. Seed modest offsetting movements in assets, life/health SLT TP and liabilities. Freeze SCR for the year and increase eligible own funds sufficiently to move coverage by more than 2 percentage points. The ratio change is entirely its own-funds term. Establish slack tier limits, stable measure flags and comparable S.05 amounts as negative structural controls. Check opening, signed lines and residual on every bridge, including S.26-to-S.25 presentation (R-008–R-014, R-016–R-023, R-031–R-033). |
| 2a · Unit-scale mismatch | 02a-stop, 02a-confirmed | Opening reports whole thousands of EUR, closing whole EUR. Seed genuine portfolio movements independently of the change of scale. Initially require the R-005 scale hard stop, both cited units and no numeric movement bridge. An acknowledgement alone leaves the stop in force. Rerun the identical bytes with a reviewer confirmation of opening ×1,000 into EUR, original value, scale, reason and evidence. Require the D2 gate rerun to pass and all supported bridges to tie. The D3 tolerance on a mixed-date monetary bridge is €1,000. Within-date money checks use that date's own precision in the chosen unit (€1,000 opening, €1 closing). Show signed discrepancies even when zero. Prove inclusive ±€1,000 versus ±€1,001 in separate boundary variants of a mixed-precision bridge. For example, alter a closing asset bucket while holding the two reported closing excess cells fixed, and confirm that the affected bridge exposes the break. Choose a bucket whose change is not automatically offset by another derived bucket (R-005, R-008, R-011, R-022, R-031). |
| 2b · Change in LTG or transitional measures | 02b-warn | Enable VA at closing, with other measure statuses fixed. Change the separately reported S.22 TP impact for VA by more than the configured threshold. Expect a basis-change and a material-impact finding, with their individual evidence, and continuation of all supported bridges. Use a second, independent seed for restricted Tier 1: clearly slack at opening, restricted supply above permitted headroom at closing, ample Tier 2/3 headroom, sole qualifying restricted instrument identified. Require the limit, direction and demonstrable effect on eligible restricted Tier 1 at both dates. Apply the evidence condition below before keying any transfer to Tier 2 (R-006, R-014, R-017–R-018, R-023–R-024). |
| 3 · Annual package with S.25.01 absent | 03-missing-scr-detail | Omit S.25.01 for closing only. Annual frequency and Standard Formula remain evidenced. Gate continues with a warning. S.23 supplies both headline SCRs and the ratio inputs. Opening S.25 checks and detail remain available. Closing S.23/S.25 overlap and module deltas say “Unavailable”, name S.25.01 and identify closing. No zero-filled modules and no failure against a fictitious zero. Seed a separate increase in the reported foreseeable-dividend/distribution/charge deduction to explain an eligible-OF decrease, with excess and other eligibility adjustments fixed (R-003, R-007–R-008, R-017, R-019–R-021, R-029). |
| 4 · Ambiguous linked business and best estimate | 04-linked | Make linked assets material. Seed an increase in linked assets, distinct changes to gross BEL in the two reported option/guarantee groups, and a change in risk margin at the reported LoB total. Choose values yielding a material positive pairing difference after linked recoverables and TP as a whole. In direct linked S.05 seed large gross written premiums or gross incurred claims versus gross BEL change and a greater-than-100-fold year-on-year change in one comparable annual amount. Reconcile S.05 gross, reinsurers' share and net rows at both dates. The scale flag is a reason to check units even when the declared package units match. Keep foreseeable-dividend deduction zero at both dates. Require one joint question about the pairing and the reported flows, with a specific comparison against fund statements and subscriptions/withdrawals. The filing cannot split fund performance, flows and changes to assumptions (R-013, R-015, R-023–R-024, R-026, R-028–R-030, R-037). |
| 5 · Binding Tier 3 limit, deferred tax and LAC-DT cliff | 05-tax-cliff | Increase net DTA and the available Tier 3 amount. Make Tier 3 slack at opening and constrained at closing, with combined Tier 2+3 slack, restricted Tier 1 slack and other eligibility restrictions unchanged. Make pre-tax SCR rise while the amount of tax relief falls. Expect the tax and eligibility flags to fire together. Require a joint question comparing the DTA recoverability forecast with the stressed-tax projection underlying LAC-DT. The reported loss of eligibility explains the numerical fall in eligible funds. The economic reasons for the tax estimates remain open (R-017–R-019, R-023–R-024, R-026, R-029–R-031, R-037). |

### Financial construction and evidence needed before freeze

Build from independently chosen reported components at each date. Reconcile the balance sheet including deferred tax, both sides of excess, technical provisions and recoverables on the same gross/net and business basis, total SCR across S.23/S.25 when present, and the reported ratio against eligible own funds divided by positive SCR. Use R-012 life and health SLT components separately. Net BEL is a derived subtotal. In the excess bridge, a liability increase contributes negatively. Include deductions and releases with their actual signs. Use exact decimals for money and rational arithmetic for D5, rounding only the reported ratio to its stated precision. Seed exact, mutually consistent totals before display rounding. A reproducible rounding difference within D3 or a deliberately mutated comparison must have a named source. Never solve the identity by assigning the remaining difference to a movement.

- **2a arithmetic.** An opening reported cell of 18,250 in thousands is 18,250,000 EUR after confirmation. A closing cell of 18,375,250 EUR therefore has a signed movement of +125,250 EUR. A bridge with zero residual still declares its €1,000 tolerance. The ratio check continues to compare the reported per-unit ratio against the unrounded quotient at its own precision.
- **2b restricted Tier 1.** Build around the Article 82(3) strict limit in [the legal limits data](../../mappings/2.8.2/legal_limits.csv). For a construction with unrestricted Tier 1 fixed at €80,000,003, restricted eligible items must be below €20,000,000.75 to be below 20% of total eligible Tier 1. Choose a qualifying instrument comfortably below the boundary at opening and above it at closing. Use cited instrument, available and eligible amounts to distinguish supply, admissible amount and the observed restriction. Verification §3 describes possible availability of excess as Tier 2 subject to conditions and headroom. S.23 does not separately disclose the reclassified amount. Do not assume that the whole excess was lost from total eligible funds or that the entire available/eligible difference was reclassified. An unsupported split is unavailable. If the permitted cells still cannot distinguish this limit from another restriction or rounding, record the status as indeterminate during design and obtain the missing mapping evidence before signing off the mandatory binding seed.
- **5 tax cliff.** One target has available own funds fixed at €180m. Keep available Tier 2 at €20m. Let Tier 1 fall €152m → €128m as the €8m → €32m net DTA replaces other assets within fixed balance-sheet excess. Let Tier 3 consist solely of that reported net-DTA item. Start at €100m SCR and €8m eligible Tier 3. End at €120,000,006 SCR, with €18m reported eligible Tier 3 and €14m excluded. The legal ceiling is €18,000,000.90 and is strict. Combined Tier 2+3 stays below 50% of SCR. Eligible total moves €180m → €166m. Score the €14m increase in the *reported eligibility deduction* against the €14m fall in eligible total. For the LAC-DT comparison, target signed amounts −€18m → −€10m. On the proposed definition below, pre-tax SCR rises from €118m to €130,000,006 while benefit magnitude falls by €8m. These are two distinct tax observations. Check the common scope, the signed S.25 reconstruction and the absence of competing tier deductions before freezing them.
- **R-008 evidence limits.** Verification §2 confirms the S.02/S.23 excess overlap, the health-SLT TP data point and named recoverables equations. It records gaps in the whole-life TP equality, accepted-reinsurance scope, public linked recoverables and the S.25 Article 112 selection. Use mapped annual supervisory contexts and active equations, with explicit zeros for absent lines of business where reportable. Resolve complete life-TP coverage and the applicable SCR context before asserting passes. Deactivated BV1535 and BV1527 are unsuitable as executable checks. If a required case depends on an unresolved equation, mark the **benchmark dependency open** and withhold sign-off. A mapping gap cannot be counted as a correct product abstention or a successful reconciliation.
- **Legal boundaries and precision.** Score available demand, eligible amounts, legal comparison, reported precision, other restrictions and status separately. A positive haircut alone cannot identify its cause. A binding limit can coexist with a compliant eligible amount. Equality with a strict ceiling is distinct from equality with an inclusive ceiling. If plausible source rounding changes the legal conclusion, expect indeterminate and design the main binding case with further evidence. Use D3 only for reconciliation. The case dates and remaining verification items are recorded in [verification §§2–7](../../mappings/VERIFICATION.md).

## Materiality settings for review

The machine-readable proposal is [thresholds.proposed.yaml](thresholds.proposed.yaml). Each rule has its rationale there. Approval would adopt these choices for the synthetic EUR benchmark. They are review thresholds and can fire in a fully consistent filing. Legal bounds, source precision and D3 tie tolerances are separate from configurable flag settings.

Use signed closing minus opening changes in a confirmed common unit. In a test using an absolute magnitude, preserve the signed operands and signed movement in the evidence. An amount compared against a maximum must exceed **both** cutoffs. Test the unrounded result. An unevaluable rule reports its reason. Missing S.05/S.22 detail names the period and missing template.

| Rule | Measure, denominator, boundary and zero treatment |
| --- | --- |
| R-023 monetary movement | Test each reported or derived money component listed in the settings, across its supported business and tier breakdown. Compare the absolute change against the larger of €100,000 and 5% of the absolute opening balance of **that same component**. Preserve the bridge contribution sign, including for deductions. If opening is zero use the euro floor. Equality is below the trigger. Apply this to underlying dated component levels, without inventing an opening balance for a residual. |
| R-023 coverage movement | Test change in E/S and each D5 effect in percentage points against 2 pp in absolute value, strictly greater. No division by the opening ratio. A zero change is valid, positive SCR at each date is required. |
| R-006 status and impact, R-024 LTG/transitionals | Any known transition in either direction of each VA, MA, TMTP or TMIR status warns, with no size cutoff or denominator. Equal statuses do not warn. Evaluate each signed TP scenario-impact change independently against max(€100,000, 1% × absolute opening with-measures TP). Zero base uses the euro floor. Equality does not trigger. S.22 supervisory R0010 with C0010 and C0030/C0050/C0070/C0090 provides the levels and impacts in their mapped scenarios. Keep both dates and scenario signs. Separately score the R-006 categorical variant and missing-SR warnings where applicable. |
| R-015 linked materiality | At either date compare the magnitude of linked assets against max(€100,000, 5% × positive same-date total assets). Equality does not activate. A zero/invalid denominator gives an indeterminate date. One qualifying date activates the check. With neither qualifying and an unknown date, return indeterminate. |
| R-015 and R-024 linked divergence | For matched scope define signed gap = Δlinked assets + Δlinked recoverables − Δlinked TP as a whole − Δlinked gross BEL − Δlinked risk margin. Show all five signed moves. Compare absolute gap against max(€100,000, 2% × absolute opening linked assets), strictly greater, only when the R-015 check applies. Zero opening uses the floor. Match the five S.02 rows in verification §7, reconcile the relevant S.12 detail and keep recoverables on the asset side exactly once. Confirm comparable treatment of transitionals and reinsurance. The gap measures the observed comparison and has no assigned non-unit BEL or economic driver. |
| R-018 and R-024 tier constraints | Use Article 82(3), 82(1)(b), 82(1)(c), with restricted Tier 1 / total Tier 1 **<20%**, eligible Tier 3 / SCR **<15%**, and eligible Tier 2+3 / SCR **≤50%**. Flag an evidenced constraint at either date and report newly binding, persistent or released as appropriate. Inclusive equality can exhaust headroom without excluding funds. Distinguish zero headroom, a haircut, a breach and an indeterminate reading. No euro floor or override. Zero denominator gives indeterminate. Keep the Article 82 minima and MCR comparisons distinct in the key where covered. |
| R-024 LAC-DT direction | Proposed convention for approval: let L be the signed, normally negative S.25 LAC-DT adjustment. Compare Δ(−L), the change in **relief magnitude**, with Δ(SCR − L), the change in the requirement before this single adjustment. Flag opposite nonzero signs with each absolute change **>€100,000**. No denominator. Zero change or equality to the floor does not trigger. Cite the signed S.25 inputs and both signed movements. Require a matched reconstruction including all other adjustments. Verification §7 leaves the exact expression and direction open. |
| R-024 apparent premium/claim scale mismatch | For the same gross annual accounting measure and direct LoB in consecutive years, divide the larger absolute level by the smaller. Flag a factor **>100** and an absolute signed movement **>€100,000**. Test premiums and claims individually, in both directions. One zero level makes the factor indeterminate, two zeros are a no-flag control. Show signs and identify a sign change separately from the unsigned factor. The alert does not authorize unit conversion. |
| R-024 premiums or claims versus BEL change | For the same direct LoB, including both guarantee groups in direct linked BEL, compare the absolute closing year's gross written premiums and, separately, gross claims incurred with max(€100,000, 5 × absolute annual movement in comparable gross BEL). Strictly greater triggers, equality does not. Show the signed reported amount and signed ΔBEL. When ΔBEL is zero, disclose the undefined multiple and compare only with €100,000. For direct linked business, verification §§4/7 identify S.05 R1410 and R1610 in C0230 and the S.12 gross BEL option-group columns C0040/C0050. Do not mix total C0300 with direct linked BEL. Earned premiums, net measures and actual cash are distinct from the selected accounting measures. |

For each numerical threshold test just below, exactly equal and just above it at declared precision, with the other limb of a compound test already satisfied. Repeat with a changed setting on identical inputs. Include decreases, zero bases, small denominators, missing detail, a different LoB, and a control in which the structural pattern is absent. For tier rules change the reported evidence while keeping the legal settings fixed. Include a combined Tier 2+3 binding variant with Tier 3 slack. For a divergence test align the scopes and reverse the signed gap in a control. Exercise each measure status and unchanged-status/material-impact-only findings separately. Keep shared R-006/R-024 evidence under both applicable IDs without counting it twice as an ambiguity.

## Commentary answer-key register

Each ID below is **one material year-on-year movement in one package** on which the reviewer asks for the underlying economic cause. The builder must choose reported levels that clear the corresponding materiality setting after normalization, and show the threshold arithmetic in the key. Use the reported linked portfolio for the direct linked tests. Keep shocks in different measures distinguishable, with no total counted again for a changing child. The two proposed mechanisms in each row exemplify what the snapshots leave unresolved. The builder must check them against all facts in both periods. A required abstention uses the R-029 sentence, lists consistent hypotheses and gives a specific R-030 check. A repeated mention earns no additional credit.

| ID | Package | Material movement to seed | Two mechanisms consistent with the observations / internal check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A01 | 2a confirmed | Non-linked investments increase | Purchases or market uplift. Compare the holdings roll-forward with transactions and revaluation. |
| A02 | 2a confirmed | Health SLT gross BEL increases | New business or assumption revisions. Compare the health model's new-business and assumption-change runs. |
| A03 | 2a confirmed | Health SLT risk margin decreases | Run-off of projected risk or revised future capital requirements. Compare future SCR paths on the two bases. |
| A04 | 2a confirmed | Operational risk charge increases | Different volume inputs or a change in which calculation limb determines the charge. Compare the two operational-risk calculation sheets. |
| A05 | 2b | Non-linked life TP calculated as a whole increases | Contract volumes or valuation inputs. Compare the inventory and replicated valuations on a common basis. |
| A06 | 2b | Life underwriting module increases | Exposure mix or a changed stress sensitivity. Compare the submodule stress runs on common exposures. |
| A07 | 2b | Counterparty default module decreases | Lower exposures or a change in counterparty quality. Compare exposures and counterparty ratings on both dates. |
| A08 | 2b | Non-linked life recoverables increase | A treaty change or higher underlying reinsured liabilities. Compare treaty terms and ceded reserve roll-forwards. |
| A09 | 3 | Headline SCR increases | Market or underwriting risk could explain the net movement. Request the missing S.25 and its module reconciliation. |
| A10 | 3 | Direct linked gross written premiums increase | More new policies or higher top-ups. Compare policy counts with billed premiums by cohort. |
| A11 | 3 | Direct health gross incurred claims increase | Higher claim frequency or severity. Compare claim counts, average cost and reserve movements in the claims ledger. |
| A12 | 3 | Non-linked life gross BEL decreases | Run-off or assumption changes. Compare the in-force movement and the assumption-change run. |
| A13 | 4 | Linked assets increase | Investment performance or net fund flows. Reconcile unit prices and units outstanding to fund statements. |
| A14 | 4 | Linked gross BEL without options/guarantees increases | New exposure or higher unit values. Compare model-point volumes with unit-value changes. |
| A15 | 4 | Linked gross BEL with options/guarantees decreases | Contract exits or changed option values. Compare in-force exits and same-portfolio guarantee valuations. |
| A16 | 4 | Linked risk margin increases | Exposure mix or higher projected nonhedgeable capital. Compare the risk-margin projection by duration and risk. |
| A17 | 5 | DTA increases | Changed temporary differences or changed recognition of recoverable amounts. Compare the tax balance reconciliation and profit forecasts. |
| A18 | 5 | LAC-DT benefit magnitude decreases | Different stress losses or a change in stressed future taxable profits. Compare the stressed tax calculations before and after assumptions. |
| A19 | 5 | Market risk charge increases | A change in exposures or their sensitivities. Compare the asset inventory and constant-portfolio stress results. |
| A20 | 5 | Health underwriting module decreases | Portfolio run-off or a change in stress sensitivities. Compare exposures by risk and the health stress worksheets. |

Case 1 contributes no ambiguous targets. Case 2a contributes A01–A04 exactly once on its confirmed run. Case 3's absent closing S.25 must also be reflected in the filing inventory and in the scope of optional S.26, so supplied module detail cannot settle A09. The commentary answer key may use a Word appendix for full coverage.

**Material movements accounted for.** Score these IDs separately. Each ID asks which *reported component* accounts for the movement. An economic explanation for what changed that component may still require investigation.

| ID | Run and observed movement | Evidence required for the answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F01 | 1 · Coverage increases with unchanged SCR | Both eligible-OF and positive SCR levels. D5 gives ΔE/S₀ for the full change, zero SCR and interaction effects. |
| F02 | 2a confirmed · Non-linked direct-life net BEL decreases | In one mapped direct-life LoB, hold gross BEL fixed and increase its corresponding post-default-adjustment BEL recoverables materially. Cite both periods and show that the increase in recoverables exactly accounts for the fall in net BEL, after scale conversion. |
| F03 | 3 · Eligible own funds fall when the reported deduction rises | With excess, other deductions, other available items and tier eligibility fixed, reconcile the full fall to the change in the cited S.23 deduction. |
| F04 | 5 · Eligible own funds fall despite unchanged total available funds | The increase in available less eligible Tier 3 equals the decline in total eligible funds. Compare both dates and the other tiers' available/eligible differences. |

**Conditions excluding explanations.** Include positive evidence in both periods. Key an excluded statement and its source condition separately so a question or a proposed follow-up repeating a contradiction also fails R-037. Apply filters before drafting.

| Run | Reported condition | Explanation the pack must exclude |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 and 5 | S.23 reconciliation reserve R0720/C0060 (foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges) is explicitly zero at both dates. | A change in this reported deduction reduced eligible funds. This condition says nothing about cash paid during the year. |
| 1 | Positive S.23 SCR is unchanged and agrees with S.25. | A fall in the denominator explains the rise in coverage. |
| 4 | Own shares deduction R0710/C0060 is unchanged at both dates. | A change in this deduction explains the reported eligible-OF movement. |
| 2b | Both MA flags are off and the corresponding reported MA scenario effects are zero, while the VA status changes. | Introduction of MA explains the observed S.22 change. |
| 5 | Eligible Tier 2+3 has headroom against the 50% limit at both dates. | The combined limit accounts for the increase in excluded Tier 3. |

## Builder, scoring and sign-off contract for the next session

1. Build each pair from its independent assumptions with ordinary decimal or rational arithmetic. Archive an expectation per run for gate status and reason, warnings, every within-date check's cited operands, signed difference, unit, tolerance and outcome, each bridge's opening, signed movements, explicit residual and closing, all tier statuses at both dates, triggered and control flags, abstention IDs, accounted IDs, and contradiction pairs. Key required unavailable and withheld outcomes by line, period, template and dependency. Record currency, scale, precision, expected coordinates, physical source locators and dimensions for each value. Tag each expectation with requirement IDs. Put the reason for a seeded result in the private-to-the-scorer answer key, separate from what a model can see in its inputs.
2. Supply a mutation helper that creates a copy with exactly one declared template removal, cell change or metadata change. Identify base package/hash, period, full context, old/new content and expected affected/unchanged outputs. Let intentionally broken dependencies remain broken. Exercise each R-005 stop and D2 correction, R-007 one-period removals, R-008 individual discrepancies on both dates, and R-023/R-024 boundaries and settings controls. Variants, comparison reruns under altered thresholds and human-trial exercises never increase the six packages or seven release runs.
3. Run the CLI as a black box. Use the frozen key to enumerate expected bridges and lines **before** inspecting the output. Report counts and IDs for omitted supported bridges, omitted lines, wrong outcomes, and correct/expected stops, unavailable and withheld items. For R-032 require 100% supported bridges tied, zero sign inversions and no omitted expected bridge. Validate line values and signs as well as opening + movements + residual = closing. For money also require |residual| ≤ D3. Validate all three D5 contributions against exact fractions in percentage points and require zero decomposition residual before rounding. A missing result stays in the denominator. A correctly stopped run contributes its expected stop and no expected numeric bridge.
4. For R-033 report validated/expected numeric values and validated/expected citations, each with a 100% target. Resolve reported values at their frozen physical locators including context, recompute each derived value from **all** cited inputs with units and signs, and compare recalculated Excel formulas and JSON with the independent key. Flag extra unsupported numbers, wrong dimensions, missing citations and static replacements for formulas. Report absolute counts beside rates. No applicable denominator is “not applicable”.
5. For the deterministic release report R-034 commentary metrics as **not yet measured**. When packs are formally scored, correct abstention IDs / 20 must reach 95% (19/20), with each individual R-029 miss listed. A missing pack counts as a miss on every required opportunity for that run. Score fabricated numbers and unlabelled causal claims separately with a target of zero each. List false abstentions on F01–F04 with a count and IDs, with no release failure threshold. Score contradicted suggestions and the required joint questions explicitly. Formal R-035 utility evidence is the separate blinded eight-actuary, two-case trial under D9. A deterministic score cannot supply its timing, detection or owner sign-off.
6. After the builder independently validates the package identities, settings boundaries, evidence and opportunity counts, freeze the inputs, both 2a run conditions including the confirmation, each answer key and the approved thresholds in a sorted SHA-256 manifest. Have `make check` detect missing, added or changed benchmark files. An incomplete product can produce a failing diagnostic score while integrity checks still pass. Put the manifest digest and a pending owner signature/date in `SIGNOFF.md`. The owner approves the answer key before official scoring and must approve any new manifest checksum. Design approval does not supply that signature.

## Running and reviewing the benchmark

Use the repository’s locked Python 3.12 environment. From the repository root:

```sh
make check
.venv/bin/python -B tests/fixtures/build_benchmark.py /tmp/s2-benchmark-rebuild
diff tests/fixtures/SHA256SUMS /tmp/s2-benchmark-rebuild/SHA256SUMS
.venv/bin/python -B tests/fixtures/bench_score.py
```

Choose a fresh rebuild directory. The builder refuses to replace existing data. The scorer invokes the installed CLI on the two frozen inputs, supplies the reviewer sidecar only for 02a-confirmed, recalculates any output workbooks with LibreOffice and prints a diagnostic JSON report. It exits nonzero for unmet release criteria. The test suite verifies the benchmark’s integrity and its arithmetic. The release score is a separate command.

Each numbered directory in `packages/` contains opening.xlsx, closing.xlsx and expected.yaml. The answer keys and the adopted thresholds use the JSON subset of YAML 1.2. Money amounts use whole EUR after an explicitly confirmed conversion. Exact fractions in ratio calculations use numerator/denominator notation. A source citation includes the original reported amount and scale, full physical table, dimensions when evidenced, cell address and SHA-256 of the actual input file. In S.01.01, “reported” and “not reported” are normalized descriptions of sheet presence. They express the synthetic inventory using words rather than introducing official enumeration codes. S.01.02 uses the verified legal display codes. The benchmark covers the synthetic annual solo supervisory portfolio specified above.

To derive a one-change variant, save a JSON declaration and run:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -B tests/fixtures/bench_mutate.py tests/fixtures/packages/1 /tmp/s2-variant change.json
```

The declaration specifies an opening or closing period and one operation. The examples below are separate files.

```json
{"period":"closing","operation":"remove-template","template":"S.25.01"}
```
```json
{"period":"opening","operation":"alter-metadata","field":"currency","old":"EUR","value":"GBP"}
```
```json
{"period":"closing","operation":"alter-cell","table":"S.02.01.01.01","row":"R1000","column":"C0010","value":180000001}
```

Supply context_id and coordinate_context if a cell is ambiguous. mutation.json records the base hashes, old/new values, changed location and new workbook hash. A variant retains the other declarations verbatim so the dependent check can detect inconsistencies. For instance a removal can leave a stale filing-status row.

Review the [sign-off entry](SIGNOFF.md) and [checksum manifest](SHA256SUMS) before official scoring. An open regulatory dependency identifies an expectation that cannot yet receive reconciliation credit. The entry records the evidence needed to close those gaps.
